planting.note: Pot up or transplant outdoors only after nights stay reliably above 50F; grow in containers and bring indoors before frost outside zone 10.

directions: This compact selection of the Brazilian tree fern, native to mountain forest understories from Brazil to Peru, is grown for dramatic new fiddleheads and fronds that unfurl in glowing red before maturing through bronze to deep glossy green. Over several years an erect rhizome slowly builds a short, thick trunk reminiscent of the tropical tree ferns it is related to. It needs warm temperatures, high humidity, and shelter from direct sun, wind, and hard frost, tolerating only brief dips near freezing before damage sets in. Consistent moisture and rich, free-draining potting mix keep the colorful new growth coming through the season, whether grown outdoors in zone 10-11 or as a container specimen elsewhere.
